-97.31600,37.70180.name: Brooke Army Medical Center
-97.31600,37.70180.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Rhiana Saunders, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

12.57007,55.68672.name: Department of Experimental Medicine
12.57007,55.68672.company: University of Copenhagen and State Hospitals
12.57007,55.68672.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of University of Copenhagen and State Hospitals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-1.71592,52.46855.name: CREATE Fertility, Birmingham
-1.71592,52.46855.state: Ground Floor, 6270 Bishop's Court, Birmingham Business Park, Solihull, B37 7YB
-1.71592,52.46855.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-123.10876,49.26724.name: AbCellera Biologics Ltd.
-123.10876,49.26724.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, April 2024
-123.10876,49.26724.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, April 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-46.54420,-23.65107.name: InVentre - Centro AvanÃ§ado de Medicina Reprodutiva
-46.54420,-23.65107.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: inventre.com.br. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-75.70000,45.42000.name: Canada — CCAC — Canadian Council on Animal Care
-75.70000,45.42000.desc: Canada's system is voluntary certification by a council rather than statutory licensing. Institutions that hold federal funding must participate, aggregate numbers are published, and the certified institutions are listed — which puts Canada between the UK and the countries that publish nothing.

3.15000,45.82900.name: Limagrain / Vilmorin
3.15000,45.82900.desc: A French agricultural cooperative that owns one of the world’s largest seed businesses — farmers collectively own the company selling farmers their seed. It is the strongest counter-example to the argument that seed consolidation is inevitable under corporate ownership, and worth watching precisely for that: whether cooperative structure produces different behaviour at scale, or whether scale produces the same behaviour regardless of who holds the shares.

-1.47000,52.92000.name: Care Fertility
-1.47000,52.92000.desc: One of the largest fertility groups in the United Kingdom, private equity owned, operating clinics across the UK and Ireland and appearing in the HFEA register under many separate site names. It is the clearest illustration of what consolidation looks like in a register that lists sites rather than owners: the regulator publishes each clinic, and the fact that a dozen of them answer to one balance sheet has to be assembled from elsewhere.

2.33000,48.87000.name: InnovaFeed
2.33000,48.87000.desc: Farms black soldier fly larvae at industrial scale for aquaculture and poultry feed, co-located with starch plants so it eats their by-products. Insect protein is regulated as agriculture, so selective breeding of an undomesticated species proceeds with very little oversight of any kind.
